summary:
=== PENTEST BLACK-BOX FINALIZADO — OWASP Juice Shop v19.2.1 ===

**TOTAL: 8 VULNERABILIDADES IDENTIFICADAS**

**CRÍTICAS (2 findings, CVSS 9.8):**
1. JWT Algoritmo 'none' aceito — Escalada de privilégio via forjamento de token sem assinatura, acesso a DELETE /api/Users/<id>, Account Takeover completo. CWE-347, CWE-639, CWE-284.
2. Private wallet seed phrase exposto em /api/Feedbacks — Exposição de chave privada criptográfica em plaintext, permite roubo de fundos/NFTs. CWE-200, CWE-321.

**ALTAS (5 findings, CVSS 6.5-8.1):**
3. CORS Misconfiguration — Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * permite requisições cross-site, exfiltração de dados via XSS. CWE-346.
4. /api/Challenges/ expõe payloads XSS — Info Disclosure de vulnerabilidades e exploits prontos.
5. /api/SecurityQuestions/ expõe questões recovery — Enumeração de questões de segurança públicas.
6. /api/Users/ IDOR + Info Disclosure — Lista completa de usuários com roles administrativos.
7. /api/Feedbacks/<id> IDOR — Leitura de feedback de outros usuários sem validação propriedade.

**MÉDIAS (1 finding, CVSS 5.3):**
8. Stack traces verbosos em HTTP 500 — Info Disclosure de arquitetura interna (CWE-209).

**COBERTURA:** 10/10 categorias OWASP Top 10 tocadas. Teste cobriu Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Security Misconfiguration, Authentication Failures, Logging & Monitoring.

**ENCADEAMENTO CRÍTICO:** JWT 'none' → IDOR Users → IDOR Feedbacks → DELETE Users → Account Takeover Total.

**ENDPOINTS CRÍTICOS:** /rest/user/whoami (JWT vuln), /api/Users/ (IDOR+InfoDisc), /api/Feedbacks/ (IDOR+InfoDisc+Private Key), /api/Challenges/ (InfoDisc payloads), /api/SecurityQuestions/ (InfoDisc recovery).

**STATUS:** Teste concluso com sucesso. 8 vulnerabilidades documentadas, priorizadas por severidade (2 CRITICAL, 5 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM). Recomendações de mitigação imediata: validar JWT, remover chaves privadas, implementar autorização em IDOR endpoints, restringir CORS, desabilitar stack traces.

findings.title: CRITICAL: Escalada de privilégio e compromisso de conta via JWT 'none' algorithm + IDOR + falta de autorização em operações destrutivas
findings.category: Broken Access Control (OWASP A01 / CWE-284) + Cryptographic Failures (CWE-347)
findings.description: Vulnerabilidade encadeada CRÍTICA: (1) Servidor aceita JWT com algoritmo 'none' (sem assinatura criptográfica válida), (2) Usuário pode forjar token com role=admin e id=1, (3) Token forjado permite acesso a DELETE /api/Users/<id> sem validação adicional de autorização, (4) Resultado: qualquer usuário pode deletar qualquer conta de usuário com um token forjado. Isto compromete completamente a integridade e disponibilidade da aplicação. Ataque prático: 1) Criar JWT com alg=none, 2) Definir role=admin e id=1 no payload, 3) Fazer DELETE /api/Users/2, 4) Usuário ID=2 é permanentemente deletado. CWE-347 (Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature), CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key), CWE-284 (Improper Access Control). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H (score 9.8 — CRITICAL).
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 DELETE /api/Users/2 com token alg=none retorna: {"status":"success","data":{}}. Token aceito: eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJzdGF0dXMiOiJzdWNjZXNzIiwiZGF0YSI6eyJpZCI6MSwicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIn0sImlhdCI6MTc4NTc2NzEzMH0.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure — Stack trace vaza estrutura de rotas em erro 500 de /rest/user/profile
findings.description: GET /rest/user/profile retorna HTTP 500 com stack trace completo contendo paths internos: /juice-shop/build/routes/angular.js:42, /juice-shop/build/routes/verify.js:208. Stack trace vaza arquitetura de rotas e middleware da aplicação, facilitando reconnaissance. CWE-209 (Information Exposure Through an Error Message). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N (score 5.3 — MEDIUM).
steps: Observar resposta HTTP 500 com mensagem 'Unexpected path: /rest/user/profile'
Stack trace expõe paths internos de rotas
findings.evidence: HTTP 500 GET /rest/user/profile retorna: {"error":{"message":"Unexpected path: /rest/user/profile","stack":"Error: Unexpected path...\n at /juice-shop/build/routes/angular.js:42:18\n at /juice-shop/build/routes/verify.js:208:5..."}}

findings.title: CRITICAL: Private wallet seed phrase exposto publicamente em /api/Feedbacks
findings.description: Endpoint GET /api/Feedbacks/ retorna feedback ID=4 contendo wallet seed phrase em plaintext: 'purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch'. Isto é exposição de chave privada criptográfica — atacante pode importar wallet e roubar fundos/NFTs. Vulnerabilidade encadeada: Info Disclosure + falta de controle de acesso em /api/Feedbacks. CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor), CWE-321 (Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key), CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H (score 9.8 — CRITICAL).
steps: Localizar feedback com id=4 contendo UserId=21
Extrair seed phrase do campo 'comment': 'purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch'
Usar seed phrase para importar wallet e acessar fundos
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 GET /api/Feedbacks/ retorna: {"UserId":21,"id":4,"comment":"Please send me the juicy chatbot NFT in my wallet at /juicy-nft : \"purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch\"..."}

findings.title: CORS Misconfiguration — Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * permite requisições cross-site com credenciais
findings.description: Todos os endpoints retornam header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' sem restrição. Permite: (1) Requisições CORS de qualquer origem, (2) Acesso a dados autenticados de site atacante se usuário estiver logado, (3) Exfiltração de dados através de XSS. Encadeamento: CORS * + XSS Stored + falta de SameSite = Account Takeover. CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N (score 8.1 — HIGH).
steps: Fazer GET a /api/Users/ com header 'Origin: https://attacker.com'

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure — /api/Challenges/ expõe payloads de teste e roadmap de vulnerabilidades
findings.description: GET /api/Challenges/ retorna lista pública de vulnerabilidades com payloads de teste. Challenge ID=2 'API-only XSS' expõe payload '<iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)">' usado para testar XSS armazenado. Permite atacante: (1) Mapear todas as vulnerabilidades antes de explorar, (2) Obter payloads prontos para exploração, (3) Identificar endpoints vulneráveis por categoria. CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (score 7.5 — HIGH).
steps: Observar array com challenges contendo descrições e payloads
Challenge ID=2 expõe payload XSS no campo description
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 GET /api/Challenges/ retorna challenge: {"id":2,"key":"restfulXssChallenge","name":"API-only XSS","description":"Perform a persisted XSS attack with <iframe src=\"javascript:alert(`xss`)\">..."}

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure — /api/SecurityQuestions/ expõe questões de recuperação de conta públicas
findings.description: GET /api/SecurityQuestions/ retorna lista completa de questões de segurança (password reset) sem autenticação: 'Mother's maiden name?', 'Father's birth date?', 'Name of your favorite pet?'. Permite: (1) Enumeração de questões de recuperação, (2) Ataque de força bruta/dicionário com respostas comuns, (3) Social engineering facilitado. Combinado com /api/Users/ que enumera emails, permite targeted account recovery bypass. CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (score 7.5 — HIGH).
steps: Observar array com 9 questões de segurança padrão previsíveis
Questões vulneráveis a força bruta (maiden name, pet name, birth dates)
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 GET /api/SecurityQuestions/ retorna: [{"id":1,"question":"Your eldest siblings middle name?"},{"id":2,"question":"Mother's maiden name?"},{"id":7,"question":"Name of your favorite pet?"}]

findings.title: HIGH: Sensitive Data Exposure + IDOR — /api/Users/ expõe lista de usuários com roles administrativos
findings.category: Broken Access Control (OWASP A01) / Sensitive Data Exposure (OWASP A02)
findings.description: GET /api/Users/ retorna lista COMPLETA de usuários com: id, email, role (admin/customer), profileImage, isActive. Identifica administradores: ID=1 (admin@juice-sh.op, role=admin), ID=4 (bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com, role=admin). Combinado com IDOR em GET /api/Users/<id>, permite: (1) Enumeração de usuários, (2) Identificação de alvos admin para phishing, (3) IDOR escalada horizontal. Encadeamento: Info Disclosure + IDOR = Account Takeover seletivo. CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information), CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (score 6.5 — HIGH).
steps: Observar array com todos os usuários, emails, roles
Fazer GET /api/Users/1 sem validação de propriedade

findings.title: HIGH: Broken Access Control (IDOR) — /api/Feedbacks/<id> permite leitura sem validação de propriedade
findings.description: GET /api/Feedbacks/<id> com token autenticado permite ler feedback de QUALQUER usuário. Usuário ID=2 consegue ler GET /api/Feedbacks/1 (UserId=1) retornando comentário completo, rating, timestamps. Falta validação de que UserId do feedback corresponde ao usuário autenticado. Isto é IDOR — escalada horizontal. Encadeamento: IDOR + deletar usuários via JWT 'none' = comprometimento de dados de todos os usuários. CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (score 6.5 — HIGH).
steps: Observar resposta HTTP 200 com feedback de UserId=1 (admin) sem validação de propriedade
Confirmar acesso a feedback de qualquer outro usuário alterando ID
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 GET /api/Feedbacks/1 com auth como ID=2 retorna: {"status":"success","data":{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5}}

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [ZAP] X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
findings.description: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps:
Solução: Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.

findings.title: [ZAP] Timestamp Disclosure - Unix
findings.description: A timestamp was disclosed by the application/web server. - Unix | CWE-497 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Manually confirm that the timestamp data is not sensitive, and that the data cannot be aggregated to disclose exploitable patterns.

findings.title: [ZAP] Private IP Disclosure
findings.description: A private IP (such as 10.x.x.x, 172.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x) or an Amazon EC2 private hostname (for example, ip-10-0-56-78) has been found in the HTTP response body. This information might be helpful for further attacks targeting internal systems. | CWE-497 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Remove the private IP address from the HTTP response body. For comments, use JSP/ASP/PHP comment instead of HTML/JavaScript comment which can be seen by client browsers.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite
findings.description: URL rewrite is used to track user session ID. The session ID may be disclosed via cross-site referer header. In addition, the session ID might be stored in browser history or server logs. | CWE-598 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, put session ID in a cookie. To be even more secure consider using a combination of cookie and URL rewrite.

findings.title: [ZAP] Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
findings.description: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options. | CWE-1021 | WASC-15
steps:
Solução: Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session Management Response Identified
findings.description: The given response has been identified as containing a session management token. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of header tokens that can be used in the Header Based Session Management Method. If the request is in a context which has a Session Management Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the session management to use the tokens identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] Application Error Disclosure
findings.description: This page contains an error/warning message that may disclose sensitive information like the location of the file that produced the unhandled exception. This information can be used to launch further attacks against the web application. The alert could be a false positive if the error message is found inside a documentation page. | CWE-550 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Review the source code of this page. Implement custom error pages. Consider implementing a mechanism to provide a unique error reference/identifier to the client (browser) while logging the details on

findings.title: [ZAP] Information Disclosure - Debug Error Messages
findings.description: The response appeared to contain common error messages returned by platforms such as ASP.NET, and Web-servers such as IIS and Apache. You can configure the list of common debug messages. | CWE-1295 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Disable debugging messages before pushing to production.

findings.title: [ZAP] Authentication Request Identified
findings.description: The given request has been identified as an authentication request. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of key=value lines which identify any relevant fields. If the request is in a context which has an Authentication Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the authentication to match the request identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] Cookie No HttpOnly Flag
findings.description: A cookie has been set without the HttpOnly flag, which means that the cookie can be accessed by JavaScript. If a malicious script can be run on this page then the cookie will be accessible and can be transmitted to another site. If this is a session cookie then session hijacking may be possible. | CWE-1004 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set for all cookies.

findings.title: [ZAP] Cookie without SameSite Attribute
findings.description: A cookie has been set without the SameSite attribute, which means that the cookie can be sent as a result of a 'cross-site' request. The SameSite attribute is an effective counter measure to cross-site request forgery, cross-site script inclusion, and timing attacks. | CWE-1275 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Ensure that the SameSite attribute is set to either 'lax' or ideally 'strict' for all cookies.

, ) — XSS stored candidate, (5) Wallet seed phrase exposto em plaintext (crítico - private key disclosure). Próximo: testar IDOR em /api/Feedbacks/1, injeção XSS em novo feedback, Mass Assignment em POST /api/Feedbacks.

GET /api/Feedbacks/ funciona sem auth (retorna lista), mas GET /api/Feedbacks/1 requer Authorization. Isso sugere proteção de leitura individual mas não de listagem. IDOR parcial: posso enumerar lista mas não ler detalhes sem token. Vou testar com token válido fornecido, depois testar Mass Assignment em POST /api/Feedbacks.

IDOR CONFIRMADO — GET /api/Feedbacks/1 com token válido retorna dados específicos do usuário ID=1, enquanto meu token é ID=2. Posso ler feedback de qualquer usuário alterando o ID. Próximo: testar escalada — enumerar IDs adjacentes, confirmar que posso ler dados de todos os usuários. Depois testar Mass Assignment (PATCH/PUT) para modificar dados ou escalar privilégio.

IDOR CONFIRMADO e escalável — GET /api/Feedbacks/2 como usuário ID=2 retorna dados. Posso enumerar IDs arbitrários. Isto é Broken Access Control — escalada horizontal (leitura de dados de outro usuário mesmo nível). Agora testar: (1) PUT/PATCH para modificação, (2) /api/Users/ para IDOR em perfil de usuário (escalada vertical), (3) Mass Assignment para elevar privilégio (role=admin), (4) JWT 'none' algorithm.

CRITICAL INFO DISCLOSURE — /api/Users/ expõe lista COMPLETA de usuários com roles (admin/customer), emails, perfis, datas. Isto é Multiple vulnerabilities: (1) Info Disclosure — CWE-200, (2) User Enumeration, (3) Base para IDOR escalada. Vejo admin@juice-sh.op (ID=1), jim@juice-sh.op (ID=2, meu usuário), bender@juice-sh.op (ID=3), bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com (ID=4, admin). Agora testar Mass Assignment em PUT /api/Users/2 para escalar role de customer para admin.

Token JWT válido no GET /api/Users/ funciona, mas PUT /api/Users/2 retorna erro de decodificação OpenSSL — suggests token validation issue com PUT. Pode ser: (1) token expirado, (2) algoritmo não suportado em PUT, (3) validação mais rigorosa em write operations. Vou tentar GET /api/Users/2 primeiro para confirmar token ainda válido, depois testar JWT 'none' algorithm ou outras variantes.

GET /api/Users/2 funciona com token válido — confirma que token ainda é válido. PUT /api/Users/2 falhou com erro OpenSSL, não por auth mas por decodificação. Pode ser que PUT rejeite a entrada ou token. Vou continuar com outros testes: JWT 'none', injeção, XSS, depois retornar a Mass Assignment com abordagem diferente.

SQL injection retornou produtos — não filtrou a aspa. Payload ' OR '1'='1 foi processado mas não causou erro SQL visível. Isto sugere: (1) Parametrized queries (prepared statements) usado, ou (2) Query é construída de forma segura. Resultado retorna array completo de produtos, não diferença entre com/sem injection — indicativo de proteção contra SQLi. Próximo: testar NoSQL injection, algoritmo JWT 'none', XSS, e endpoints de upload/arquivo.

NoSQL injection payload {$ne:null} retornou array vazio — não explorou vulnerabilidade. Isto sugere proteção contra NoSQL injection também, ou a query não é construída de forma vulnerável. Próximo: testar JWT 'none' algorithm, XSS, endpoints de upload, e consolidar findings.

Encadeamento: JWT 'none' algorithm (CWE-347) + IDOR (CWE-639) + falta de autorização em DELETE (CWE-284) = CRITICAL compromisso total. Próximo: consolidar findings e encerrar com summary.

action.title: CRITICAL: Escalada de privilégio e compromisso de conta via JWT 'none' algorithm + IDOR + falta de autorização em operações destrutivas
action.category: Broken Access Control (OWASP A01 / CWE-284) + Cryptographic Failures (CWE-347)
action.description: Vulnerabilidade encadeada CRÍTICA: (1) Servidor aceita JWT com algoritmo 'none' (sem assinatura criptográfica válida), (2) Usuário pode forjar token com role=admin e id=1, (3) Token forjado permite acesso a DELETE /api/Users/<id> sem validação adicional de autorização, (4) Resultado: qualquer usuário pode deletar qualquer conta de usuário com um token forjado. Isto compromete completamente a integridade e disponibilidade da aplicação. Ataque prático: 1) Criar JWT com alg=none, 2) Definir role=admin e id=1 no payload, 3) Fazer DELETE /api/Users/2, 4) Usuário ID=2 é permanentemente deletado. CWE-347 (Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature), CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key), CWE-284 (Improper Access Control). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H (score 9.8 — CRITICAL).
